title: Velocity at 0.1s
description: Essential: Correctly calculates v = gt = 1 m/s for the first 0.1 seconds of free fall.

title: Displacement in second 0.1s
description: Essential: Correctly computes Δx = ½g(t₂² - t₁²) = 0.15 m for the interval from t=0.1s to t=0.2s.

title: Streak length ratio K
description: Essential: Derives and states K = √2 ≈ 1.414 as the ratio of streak lengths at 10 cm vs 5 cm below exit.

title: Free-fall kinematics application
description: Important: Uses v² = 2gh to relate velocity to fall distance for the streak analysis.

title: Time interval handling
description: Important: Correctly distinguishes between displacement during a specific time interval versus total displacement.

title: Phenomenon explanation
description: Optional: Explains that streaks form due to finite camera exposure time capturing motion blur.

title: Unit consistency
description: Optional: Maintains consistent units (m, s, m/s) throughout calculations.

title: Sign or direction error
description: Pitfall: Uses incorrect sign for displacement or velocity direction in free fall.

title: Confusing displacement formulas
description: Pitfall: Attempts to compute second-interval displacement using Δx = v₀t + ½gt² without adjusting for initial velocity at t=0.1s.

title: Incorrect streak ratio
description: Pitfall: Assumes streak length is proportional to height rather than velocity (K = 2 instead of √2).
